text:
maya: alert from deploy-bot — hosted-api p99 spike + queue depth increase in us-west-2, started ~2165999900. anyone oncall?

igor: I'm on. seeing p95 jump from 120ms -> 480ms and p99 ~1.2s on text-generate route. queues hit 600 requests queued on a handful of shards.

sam: deploy-bot posted kernel-fallback events in the last 3m: many calls choosing 'aux-kernel' instead of fast-gpu kernels. logs show kernel selector falling back due to batch-size=1 prevalance.

courtney: that's odd — we rolled batch-sampler rebalancing last night (A/B) to favor latency for small requests. could be interacting with kernel selector heuristics.

li: looking at KV cache hit ratio — it's dropped from 82% -> 26% on affected shards. evictions spiked at same time. suspect noisy-tenant churn causing cache degeneracy.

igor: stack trace + selector log snippet: ```INFO kernel_selector: chosen=aux-kernel reason='batch_size_small' fallback=true kernel_latency_est=78ms cpu_cost=high``` lots of fallback events.

sam: profiler output (aggregate 60s) shows GPU utilization low (~22%) but CPU spike on kernel marshalling layer. aux-kernel is CPU-bound.

maya: so hypothesis: batch-sampler rebalancer caused many 1-2 token micro-batches => kernel selector prefers aux-kernel or CPU path => KV cache degenerates due to cache thrash from noisy tenant => more priming requests => more small batches. feedback loop.

courtney: agree. also saw rate-limiter backpressure toggling; there are per-tenant burst quotas that fire when queues grow which can create head-of-line blocking for multi-request tenants.

li: attaching short perf counters I pulled: top hot functions are prepare_io(), kv_evict(), kernel_serialize(). I can post flamegraphs to #eng-runtime-profiling.

igor: mitigation options: 1) temporarily disable batch-sampler rebalancer A/B for hosted prod route, 2) bump small-batch kernel preference to favor fast kernels up to batch_size=4, 3) throttle noisy tenant(s) at ingress.

sam: also can enable prefix-KV caching warmup for affected shards to avoid cold priming. but that's longer.

maya: can we do (1) now? who has perms to flip A/B?

courtney: I can flip flag and roll back the rebalancer. doing it now.

deploy-bot: rollout started for feature flag "batch_sampler_rebalancer" -> off. 3/3 targeted hosts updated.

igor: after flip: queue depth down from 600 -> 120 in ~30s, p95 trending back to ~140ms, p99 to ~300ms. Kernel-fallback events decreased by ~87%.

li: KV hit ratio recovering slowly; priming still happening but evictions are lower.

maya: great. let's open a short postmortem and track long-term fixes: a) refine kernel-selector heuristics for small-batch tradeoffs, b) make sampler rebalancer aware of kernel profiles, c) tougher noisy-tenant isolation and per-shard kv quotas, d) monitor autoswitch thresholds with synthetic load.

sam: I'll own kernel-selector change (RFC + canary). courtney will own sampler feature changes, li will work on kv isolation. igor keeps monitoring for 1h and will escalate if regressions.

maya: thanks all. created incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/2166000000-aux-kernel-fallback — add notes. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: incident created by maya — incident ID INC-2166000000

igor: closing thread, keeping watch.
